- Stye. A stye is a red, painful bump on the eyelid caused by a blocked oil gland.

- Dry eye. Oil and flakes can build up in your tear film (a thin layer of tears across the surface of your eye). This can make your eyes feel dry. Or your eyes may feel watery or teary because your tears aren’t working correctly.

Posterior blepharitis affects the outside of the inner edge of the eyelid [nei_007_chunk_03].

Risk factors include dandruff, rosacea, oily skin, and allergies affecting eyelashes [nei_007_chunk_02].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.

Eye doctors can check for Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) as part of a comprehensive dilated eye exam [nei_020_chunk_03]. This exam involves eye drops to dilate the pupil, followed by an eye exam to check for RP and other eye problems [nei_020_chunk_03]. The exam includes a visual field test to assess peripheral vision [nei_020_chunk_03].

Other tests used to diagnose RP are electroretinography (ERG), which measures how well the retina responds to light [nei_020_chunk_03]; optical coherence tomography (OCT), which uses light waves to image the retina [nei_020_chunk_03]; and fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging [nei_020_chunk_03].

Genetic testing is also an option to learn more about the type of RP and how symptoms may progress [nei_020_chunk_03].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.
